newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK smashes racket smuggling stolen cars into China.
newsitem.headline: HK smashes racket smuggling stolen cars into China.

text.p: Hong Kong's graft busters said on Tuesday they had smashed a smuggling ring which had been trafficking stolen vehicles from the British colony into China for a year.

The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said it had arrested 14 men, including a senior customs officer and a retired chief customs officer, for alleged corruption relating to the racket.
"This group of people we think has been running together for the best part of 12 months," an ICAC officer told government radio.

"We believe that one of the customs officers was turning a blind eye at the customs post as vehicles passed through there, and also perhaps accessing (a) computer database to see whether or not the vehicles were on any kind of wanted list," he said.
Two workmen serving with Customs and Excise who were allegedly obtaining documents for the gang were also arrested, he said.
A stolen 24-seat van was also recovered in the operation, government radio reported. The detained men were not identified.
